summary.text: PLA Aero is a foaming, lightweight polylactic acid. Makers sell it for RC planes, drones, gliders and figurines, and describe a matt surface. It is amorphous as printed, so it softens at its glass transition: its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 53 °C. On the H2C it prints at 195⁠–⁠250 °C, and makers say the foaming depends on the printing temperature.

items.text: Ideal material for model airplanes
Lightweight polyactide is a polymer that expands during 3D printing.
With the active foaming technology, parts can be achieved with a weight reduction of up to 70%.
With a spool of LW-PLA you can print up to 3 times more parts than with a spool of standard PLA due to the reduced flow factor
Can become soft again from 60 degrees
Thread formation during empty runs can practically not be prevented
Color becomes paler after expansion
From a temperature of approx. 200 ° C, the material begins to foam.
The expansion effect increases with increasing temperature.

The maximum expansion is achieved at a printing temperature of approx. 250-260 ° C. With optimal settings, the flow factor can be reduced to a value of 0.3, which leads to extremely light PLA components.
A heating bed is advantageous for LW-PLA filament, but not absolutely necessary.
Reduce flow or extrusion multiplier
The optimal extrusion multiplier must be determined by means of tests.

items.text: The LW-PLA-HT is an excellent filament for printing RC Planes, Cosplay, and other light weight items.
Light Weight PLA-HT has a formulation featuring an increased temperature resistance compared to generic LW-PLA.
Thinly printed structures will be able to handle heat from external sources at prologues exposure.
For printing thin structure (such as for RC plane parts), it is recommended to print the first layer at 100% flow using 200˚C nozzle temperatures.
Increasing the temperature for the second layer (roughly 235˚C) to activate the foaming, and reduce the flow to 50-60% for maximum results.

Under the same model and at the same speed, the lightweight PLA enables the model aircraft to have a lighter wing load and a lower stall speed, which can greatly improve the performance of the model aircraft.

items.text: Lightweight PLA is a type of lightweight 3D printing material specially developed for aircraft model, ship model, drone and other fields.
Lightweight PLA is a PLA filament that will start foaming with the aid of a blowing agent during the printing process.
With this technique, it is easy to reduce the weight of the model.
In the best-case scenario, the model weight can be reduced to 50% of a model printed with ordinary PLA.
Since Light Weight PLA adopts the "On-Demand foaming" technology, the filament will continue to expand in the nozzle after being heated during the printing process.
Therefore, it will cause unavoidable stringing during the nozzle movement.
E ven adjusting the retraction setting in the slicing software cannot solve this problem.
In addition to that, the matte texture of the printed surface can reduce the visibility of printed layers and thus give a smooth surface finish.
During the printing process by adjusting the printing temperature, the foaming ratio of the blowing agent can be easily controlled.
Based on the above, it is recommend ed to turn off the retraction setting.
The string on the surface of models can easily be removed by hand.
